entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.76 of 2023 registered at Police Station Alampur, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences punishable under Section 363, added Sections 366, 376,
34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 04-10-2023.
As per the case of prosecution, father of victim reported to PS Alampur, District Bhind that his daughter, aged around 17 years and 8 months, is missing since night of 24-09-2023.
Some unknown person has allured and taken his minor daughter.
On such allegations, PS Alampur, District Bhind registered FIR at Crime No.76 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against unknown offender.
Victim was recovered from Chakla Gate, Outpost Metad, PS Gotad, (Gujarat) on Sanjeev Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4236154/

sentences.text: . In her statement recorded under Section 161 of CrPC on 04-10-2023, victim stated that her uncle introduced her with one Sanjeeev Kushwah (applicant).
She used to converse with Sanjeev Kushwah on mobile phone.
On 22-09-2023, she called Sanjeev Kushwah and requested him to take her along with him otherwise she would die.
On 24-09- 2023, her uncle brought some sleep pills.
She administered those sleep pills in food of family in the night.
Her uncle assisted her to reach Sanjeev Kushwah, who was waiting for her near the tower of Village.

Her uncle told them that she should go with Sanjeev Kushwah on motorcycle and they may marry in Court, therefore, she went with Sanjeev Kushwah to Alampur and from there, they boarded a four-wheeler along with some other persons and went to Kota (Rajasthan).

Sanjeev Kushwah took her to Udaipur, but mid-way,
they deboarded bus and went to Tilakwada.
They stayed with paternal aunt of Sanjeev Kushwah for two days at there.
Applicant Arti Ben, happens to be daughter-in-law of paternal aunt of Sanjeev Kushwah,
took them to her paternal home in Bota (Gujarat).
Her father, uncle and police team reached there and brought her to Alampur, District Bhind.
She further stated that Sanjeev Kushwah has allured and taken her to Badodra (Gujarat) for marring her, but he or any other persons have not committed any wrong or indecent act with her.
Later, in her statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, victim alleged rape against her uncle and molestation against Sanjeev Kushwah and his associates Pawan and Ajay.

Applicant- accused Sanjeev Kumar Kushwah, other co- accused Pawan,
Raju alias Rajkumar, Lakhan Patwa and Ajay Kushwah were arrested on 04-10-2023.
Applicant is in custody ever since.
Statements of witnesses have also been recorded.
Relevant seizure has been made.
Medico- legal examination of victim and applicant has been conducted.
Later on, offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act was added.
Investigation is underway.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that as per prosecution story, victim is aged 17 years and 8 months.
Applicant Sanjeev Kumar Kushwah is aged 19 years.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons.
Applicant was not aware about the minority of victim and consequence of their acts.

In her initial statement, victim has not alleged any misdemeanour against the applicant but later under the pressure of family, she had made general allegation of molestation (Chheda-Chhedi) against the applicant.
Applicant is a labourer by profession.
Both the parties belong to same socio-economic status, therefore, there is no likelihood of his tampering with the evidence.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving behind his family and home.
No further custodial interrogation is required in the matter against the applicant as the investigation with regard to the applicant is almost complete.
Jail incarceration on false allegation is causing hardship to the applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be released on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State ably assisted by learned Counsel for the complainant,
opposed the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned Counsel submits that the applicant is the person who has allured and taken the victim, therefore, he may not be extended the benefit of bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, regard being had to the young age of the applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release Sanjeev Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4236154/
2 the applicant on bail.

The applicant shall ensure due compliance of provisions of Section 309 of Cr.P.C regarding examination of witness in attendance;
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective without reference to the Court.
